label: D1 after a rewarded common trial when the agent is about to choose a2 (S2-is-good, win-stay on a2), first ~70 trials of the episode
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), and almost only when the reward input is 1 (99.4% of mass). It is further restricted to trials where the agent is about to choose a2 (upcoming choice, which the agent computes; prev_action is a2 in ~all active cases, i.e. win-stay on a2), and is silent when the rewarded previous trial had a rare transition (prev_common=0: 0.1% of mass; e.g. a2 -> S1 rewarded gives ~0.02). It essentially never fires after episode trial ~72, a time-in-episode cutoff. Good state is S2 in 80% of active mass. The model policy logit at D1 is in a moderate a2-preferring band [-4.4, -1.5] for 99.9% of activations; using that band instead of action==2 raises dev F1 to 0.93, but I recorded the behavioral version (dev P 0.80, R 0.94, F1 0.86, mass recall 0.99). It does not fire on unrewarded D1s, on a1 choices, or on any GO/D2 step. No uses of future random outcomes. Magnitude claims not checked beyond: the lowest activation quartile holds most misses.

issues: Most factual claims hold on dev. The feature fires only at D1 (GO and D2 have 0 active steps). in_rew=1 holds 0.994 of activation mass. action=2 holds 1.000 (12 active steps with a1). prev_common=0 holds 0.001. Rate by ep_trial falls steeply: precision of the choice-band predicate is 0.86 at trials 60-65, 0.79 at 66-69, 0.61 at 70-71, 0.31 at 72-74 and 0.003 at 75+. good=S2 holds 0.80 of mass. choice < -1.52 holds 0.999.

Systematic false-positive class in the recorded predicate. Where the predicate is true but the D1 policy logit is choice >= -1.52, there are 11,064 predicted steps (dev) at only 1.7% precision. That is about 10.9k of the ~16.1k false positives, so roughly two thirds of all false positives are one identifiable class, not scattered noise. 'About to choose a2' is a loose proxy. The feature tracks a strong, committed a2 preference at D1.

Related history signature: when the trial two back was unrewarded (tv('reward',-2)==0), the recorded predicate's precision falls to 0.51 (12,011 predicted), against 0.93 when it was rewarded. When good=S1, precision is 0.53. The feature needs accumulated confidence in a2 (a rewarded streak, S2 good), not just one rewarded a2 trial. The label's 'win-stay on a2' undersells this.

The explainer knew about this gap: they found that the choice band raises F1 to 0.93, but recorded the weaker action==2 version, and the label still says just 'about to choose a2'. With a clear systematic counterexample class left, the recorded predicate and label should not be upheld as is.

Minor: prev_common != 0 includes prev_common == -1 (the window's first trial, 24% of mass). So the label's 'after a rewarded common trial' is stated as 'not after a rare trial' in the predicate. Calling the trial-~72 cutoff a time-in-episode effect is accurate; trials 70-79 still hold 0.5% of mass.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after a rewarded trial (not following a rare transition) when the agent is already strongly committed to a2 (policy logit a1-a2 < ~-1.5, typically after a rewarded a2 streak with S2 good), in roughly the first 70 trials of the episode
